entries.title: DICEBITS
entries.description:
A falling-block puzzle game with dice. Pairs of dice drop into a 7×7 grid, and touching dice of the same value disappear once the group is at least as large as the number they show: two 2s, three 3s, four 4s and so on. A 1 never matches on its own, but when a 1 touches a group being cleared, every 1 on the grid goes with it. A full straight from 1 to 6 in a row or column clears for a bonus, and dice falling into new groups set off chains worth more with each wave.

The pace rises over 20 levels, and new elements appear along the way: random dice that change face as they fall, bricks that only special dice can remove, seekers that clear every die of one value, bombs, crosses that clear a row and column, and, from level 7, junk drops from the top of the grid. The game ends when a die is left in the top row.

This is the free demo of the full game.

Controls: Left and Right move the pair, Down soft-drops and Up hard-drops. A and B rotate, L and R hold or swap the pair, Select shows the grid lines and Start pauses. L+R+Select puts the game to sleep, and A+B+Start+Select resets it.

Your lantern is your shield and your life: wraiths drift toward you through the dark but cannot enter the light, and your oil burns down with every step. Push braziers and bone slabs, time the skeletons' patrols, freeze the gloomweavers in bright light, slip the Wardens' killing gaze, cross rivers of blood, lava, and acid - each with its own rule - and ring bell portals across the room. entries.title: Minitris
entries.description:
A logic puzzle game for the Game Boy and Game Boy Color, based on the original Minitris by Michal Ursiny and UCI Software. It is not a Tetris clone: there are no tetrominoes and no rotation. Single coloured cells drop one at a time into a 4×12 well, and lining up 3 or more of the same colour horizontally, vertically or diagonally clears them. The remaining cells fall under gravity and can form new lines, chaining into cascades that multiply the score. The game speeds up every 45 cleared cells, up to level 21. Features a Top 5 high score table and lifetime statistics saved to battery-backed SRAM, colour palettes on GBC and high-contrast patterned cells on DMG, and 3 selectable tracks by MuteAudio (hUGEDriver) with 12 sound effects (CBT-FX).

Controls: Left/Right moves the cell, Down or A hard drops it, Start pauses, Select toggles mute.

A music album packaged as a cassette tape. It plays in TAPE DECK 02, a cassette-deck player program by RK-G Media Works, and was built with their TAPE FACTORY tool, which turns your own audio files into tape ROMs like this one.

All the music is public domain or CC0. Side A has chiptune arrangements of public-domain scores from the Mutopia Project: Bach's Prelude in C (BWV 846) and Invention 13 (BWV 784), Joplin's The Entertainer and Pineapple Rag, and Debussy's Arabesque No. 1 and Clair de lune. Side B has piano recordings from The Open Goldberg Variations by Kimiko Ishizaka (2012, CC0): the Aria, Variations 1, 7 and 30 (Quodlibet), and the Aria da Capo. The TAPE DECK 02 player itself is closed source.

Controls: A plays or pauses, B stops, Left and Right skip tracks, Up and Down change the volume, holding L or R rewinds or fast-forwards, Select changes the play mode and holding Select flips the tape to the other side.

entries.title: Orion GB
entries.description:
A turn-based 4X space strategy game. Starting from a single world, you explore the galaxy, found colonies, research technologies, trade, and make peace or war with rival empires. You win by conquering every rival, or by winning the vote of the galactic council, held every 20 turns, to become Supreme Leader. It is an unofficial, non-commercial fan demake inspired by Master of Orion, with its own mechanics.

There are six playable races, each with its own portrait, personality and theme music, and you face a random draw of 1 to 5 rivals that you only discover when you meet them. Galaxies come in four sizes (16 to 48 systems) and three map types: the hand-built Lattice, a two-armed Spiral, or a Random galaxy. Each planet's output is split between ships, defense, industry, ecology and research. There are 64 technologies in four research trees, planet modules such as shipyards, banks and shields, and, since version 1.2, a Ship Design screen for building custom ships from hull slots and tech-unlocked modules. Rival empires also make their own wars, peace deals and alliances with each other. The game uses an MBC5 cartridge with a battery-backed save and autosave.

The author notes that AI balance has mostly been tested by bots, and that games can last hundreds of turns. Saves from 1.12.2 do not load in 1.2, so 1.12.2 is also provided for continuing older games.

Controls: the D-pad, A, B, Start and Select. Each screen shows its buttons along the bottom.

entries.title: Waternet
entries.description:
A pipe-connecting puzzle game based on the Net and Netslide puzzles from Simon Tatham's Portable Puzzle Collection. In every mode the goal is to connect all the pipes so that water can flow through them from the source. There are three game modes: Rotate, where each pipe is turned in place; Slide, where whole rows and columns are shifted using the arrows around the board; and Roslid, which combines both. Each mode has five difficulties with 25 levels each, for 375 levels in total, plus a Random difficulty that generates endless new levels. An in-game help section explains the rules of each mode.

Runs on both the Game Boy and the Game Boy Color, with colour graphics on GBC and a Super Game Boy border. Progress is saved to battery-backed SRAM. The game was also released for the Game Gear, Master System, Analogue Pocket and Mega Duck.

Controls: A or Start confirms in menus and rotates or slides while playing, B goes back.
